items.summary: In an order filed October 30, 2026, Judge Ryan T. Holte of the United States Court of Federal Claims dismissed without prejudice a pro se complaint filed August 10, 2026 for failure to prosecute under Rule 41(b) of the Rules of the Court of Federal Claims. The order states that the plaintiff neither paid the filing fee nor submitted a completed in forma pauperis application by the September 21, 2026 deadline set in an August 20, 2026 order. Court mailings to the address listed on the complaint envelope were returned as undeliverable, and the Clerk was directed to enter judgment.
items.title: PRAIRIE v. USA

items.summary: In an order of dismissal filed October 30, 2026, Judge Armando O. Bonilla of the United States Court of Federal Claims dismissed a pro se complaint for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction. The court found that, although the United States was named as defendant, the complaint asserted allegations only against individuals, including state and local officials and judicial officers, related to a Harris County, Texas state criminal prosecution, and identified no non-frivolous substantive claim against the United States. The order notes that a related complaint filed in the Southern District of Texas had previously been dismissed.

items.summary: In a Memorandum Opinion and Order filed October 30, 2026, the United States Court of Federal Claims granted the Government's motion to dismiss a pro se complaint by a federal inmate seeking more than $100,000 under the Federal Tort Claims Act. The complaint alleged that United States Marshals Service and Bureau of Prisons personnel lost the plaintiff's hearing aids during a January 2023 transfer and that the Bureau of Prisons refused to replace them. The court held that the Tucker Act excludes tort claims from its jurisdiction and declined to transfer the case to a federal district court because the United States has not waived sovereign immunity for claims arising from alleged negligent loss of inmate property.

__________________________________________

PAMELA DE
items.summary: In a non-precedential opinion in No. 26-3216, In re: Wells Fargo COVID Forbearance Settlement Litigation, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit affirmed the Southern District of Ohio's denial of motions by Kenneth and Kayla Rogers to intervene under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 24(a)(2) and its denial of their request for an evidentiary hearing. The court found that the Rogerses did not meet the substantial legal interest requirement because, under the approved settlement's class definition, they are not class members, and it noted that the settlement had already been approved and payments had begun when intervention was sought. The court did not decide whether the district court abused its discretion in finding the motions timely.

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit affirmed summary judgment for Everest Indemnity Insurance Company, Bearing Insurance Group, and EverSports & Entertainment Insurance in a suit brought by Sinmier, LLC as a mortgagee. Applying Ohio law, the court held that the settlement agreement and deed in lieu of foreclosure extinguished Sinmier's insurable mortgagee interest once the mortgage debt was released. Because each of Sinmier's claims depended on that interest, the court found the claims fail as a matter of law.

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit reversed the Southern District of Ohio's dismissal of the Estate of Elijah Isham's Section 1983 complaint and remanded the case. The district court had treated the complaint as a legal nullity because it was initially filed by the administrator without counsel. The court found no abuse of discretion in the denial of reconsideration, and it addressed under 28 U.S.C. § 1654 whether a pro se filing on behalf of an estate can be cured by later retaining counsel.

items.summary: The Tenth Circuit affirmed a United States Tax Court decision rejecting the challenges of Scott and Audrey Blum to IRS notices of deficiency for tax years 1999, 2007, and 2010, which disallowed a $78.5 million tax shelter loss and assessed about $22 million in taxes and penalties. The Blums had argued that the IRS's partnership-level determination was untimely, and the Tax Court held that they waived that argument by not raising it in the partnership-level proceeding in the Northern District of California. The opinion, by Circuit Judge Matheson, describes the two-level TEFRA framework for partnership items and affected items under the Internal Revenue Code.

items.summary: Dated November 3, 2026, this proclamation by President Donald J. Trump declares that the solar system and all of outer space beyond Earth are the province of all humans and are open to exploration, development, use, and the establishment of a permanent presence by American citizens, consistent with United States law and the international obligations of the United States. The text recounts that the Artemis II mission carried astronauts around the Moon in April, states that Artemis III is planned for the following summer, and sets a goal of returning to the Moon by 2028. It also references executive orders and directives on human spaceflight and the commercial space industry, and affirms the intent of the United States to lead in space exploration.
items.title: THE AMERICAN DECLARATION OF FREEDOM IN SPACE

items.summary: In an opinion filed November 2, 2026, the Ninth Circuit held that San Jose Police Officer James Adgar is entitled to qualified immunity on Kyle Johnson's Fourth Amendment excessive force claim under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, and reversed the district court's denial of Adgar's post-verdict motion for judgment as a matter of law on that claim, with Judge Paez dissenting in part. The panel found that substantial evidence supported a finding that Adgar violated the Fourth Amendment by firing a 40mm projectile impact weapon indiscriminately into a crowd, and it concluded that the precedent Nelson v. City of Davis was materially distinguishable. The panel remanded for recalculation of attorneys' fees, directed the district court to defer that recalculation until it decides the Bane Act claim, and in a concurrently filed order certified a question on the Bane Act standard to the California Supreme Court.

items.summary: In a nonprecedential order dated November 2, 2026, the Seventh Circuit vacated the district court's summary judgment for the Department of the Interior and the Fish and Wildlife Service in Robert Aland's Freedom of Information Act suit and remanded for further proceedings. The court held that Aland failed to exhaust administrative remedies for his request to the Fish and Wildlife Service, which it treated as a separate request from the one sent to the Office of the Secretary. items.summary: In a nonprecedential order dated November 2, 2026, the Seventh Circuit affirmed summary judgment for Inguran, LLC in Li Men's suit under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act. The court concluded that the record did not support a finding that Inguran terminated Men because of her age or in retaliation for her complaint to human resources, and that the company's stated performance reasons were not shown to be pretextual. The court also noted that it applies the Supreme Court's Muldrow standard, under which a plaintiff must show only some injury to employment terms or conditions, to ADEA discrimination claims, and stated that this standard did not change its outcome.

items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 90-19-02, which applies to all MD Helicopters, LLC (type certificate previously held by McDonnell Douglas Helicopter Company) Model 369, 369A, 369D, 369E, 369F, 369FF, 369H, 369HE, 369HM, and 369HS, helicopters, that are equipped with a cargo hook. AD 90-19-02 requires replacing the overrunning clutch assembly and sprag assembly with airworthy parts and repetitively inspecting the sprag assembly, clutch inner and outer races of the overrunning clutch assembly. Since the FAA issued AD 90-19-02, after further analysis the FAA determined that additional helicopter models are affected by this unsafe condition. This proposed AD would expand the applicability and would require removing certain overrunning clutch assemblies and certain overrunning clutch subassemblies from service, installing or replacing parts, and reidentifying certain overrunning clutch assemblies, as applicable. items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES Office of the Secretary 45 CFR Part 84 RIN 0945-AA27 Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance AGENCY: Office for Civil Rights (OCR)
items.summary: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS or Department) issues this rule to revise the regulation implementing section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (section 504) as it applies to recipients of HHS funding (entitled “Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance,” (“2024 Final Rule”)), published on May 9, 2024. This rule clarifies that the Department interprets the statutory exclusion of “gender identity disorders not resulting from physical impairments” from the terms “individual with a disability” and “disability” set forth in our regulations to encompass “gender dysphoria not resulting from a physical impairment” for purposes of the regulation. This clarification is necessary to resolve ambiguity introduced in the preamble to the 2024 Final Rule and to ensure compliance with the best reading of the governing statute.
tags: department of health and human services
items.title: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 42 CFR Part 486 [CMS-3409-F] RIN 0938-AU54 Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Organ Procurement Organizations Conditions for Coverage: Revisions to the Conditions
items.summary: This final rule revises the Conditions for Coverage for Organ Procurement Organizations (OPOs) to clarify outstanding procedural questions and provide additional operational flexibility for OPOs to achieve high performance resulting in the successful procurement, distribution, and transplantation of more life-saving organs. This rule revises definitions, revises the designation requirements for OPOs, clarifies when an OPO's service area is open for competition, and updates the process for appeals. We are committed to holding all OPOs accountable for their performance and this final rule does not revise the focus on improving the volume of donors and transplants assessed in the outcome measures or the tier structure used for re-certification and de-certification of OPOs.

items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-17-03, which applies to certain Embraer S.A. Model ERJ 190-100 STD, -100 LR, -100 IGW, and -100 ECJ airplanes; and Model ERJ 190-200 STD, -200 LR, and -200 IGW airplanes. AD 2024-17-03 requires revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-17-03, the FAA has determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would continue to require certain actions in AD 2024-17-03 and would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-11821; Project Identifier AD-2026-00567-T] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes AGENCY: Federal Aviation Admini
items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-25-09, which applies to certain The Boeing Company Model 757 airplanes. AD 2024-25-09 requires installing new relays and changing certain wire bundles leading to the power transfer unit (PTU) control valve. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-25-09, the FAA determined that the requirements bulletin mandated by AD 2024-25-09 contains errors. In some cases, those errors prevent the actions required by AD 2024-25-09 from being fully accomplished. In other cases, the errors would allow actions that could introduce new hazards affecting the operation and thus the availability of the PTU. This proposed AD would require, depending on the airplane configuration, installing new relays and new connectors, changing certain wire bundles, doing an operational test, and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Helicopters Model AS350B2, AS350B3, and EC130B4 helicopters. This proposed AD would require modifying and reidentifying an affected fuse cover and would prohibit installing an affected fuse cover on any helicopter. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.opening_verbatim: IB Union Calendar No. 764 119th CONGRESS 2d Session H. R. 8347 [Report No. 119–867] IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES April 16, 2026 Mr. Owens introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce Novem
items.summary: H.R. 8347, the Reinforcing Underserved, Rural, and Local Healthcare Act (RURAL Healthcare Act), was introduced April 16, 2026, by Mr. Owens and referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, then reported with an amendment on November 2, 2026. The reported text would provide that a qualified locum tenens professional or advanced care practitioner is not considered an employee of the entity receiving temporary services under the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 and the National Labor Relations Act. The bill defines qualified individuals as physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, or certified registered nurse anesthetists providing services for no more than one continuous year at a single site under a written contract stating they will not be treated as employees.
items.title: 119 HR 8347 RH: Reinforcing Underserved, Rural, and Local Healthcare Act

items.summary: H.R. 8660, the Valuing Employee Stock Today Act (VEST Act), was introduced May 4, 2026, by Mr. Mackenzie and referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, then reported with an amendment on November 2, 2026. The reported text amends section 7(e)(8) of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to include restricted stock unit programs in the exemption for equity income from the regular rate calculation for overtime, and changes "exercise" to "exercise or acceptance" in subparagraph (C). The amendments would take effect 90 days after enactment, and the bill limits employer liability for certain restricted stock unit grants obtained before the effective date, within a 12-month period under specified conditions, or under a collective bargaining agreement in effect on that date.
items.title: 106 HR 8660 RH: Valuing Employee Stock Today Act
